decision: Partitioned for FPGA prototype with a soft-CPU controller and external GPU/CPU-hosted surrogate execution. The surrogate remains in software/gpu_service, while FPGA RTL implements transport, partitioning, supervision, clamping, timeout handling, and safe fallback. Hardware-deployable logic is limited to bounded control/safety functions; the physics surrogate itself is not assigned to FPGA because the model qualification requires a remote GPU worker and no evidence proves RTL deployment readiness.
decision_factors: Model qualification indicates the selected surrogate is remote_nim and requires a GPU worker; inference was not executed and accuracy was not qualified, so the surrogate must remain in software/gpu_service.
The contract explicitly forbids assuming pretrained inference availability and requires transparent, referenceable baseline behavior.
The architecture already separates the soft CPU firmware from RTL safety logic and keeps the DoMINO surrogate outside the FPGA.
The implementation path is fpga_prototype, which favors a deterministic hardware safety shell plus firmware orchestration rather than full model acceleration in RTL.
Safety requirements demand stale-data rejection, timeout handling, command clamping, and safe fallback with deterministic hardware behavior.
The system must support resource-constrained embedded control, but the physics model itself is not proven hardware-deployable.
The FPGA interface constraints favor bounded streams and register windows, matching transport/supervision rather than tensor or flow-field compute.
ASIC reuse is possible for the control shell only; the surrogate remains external until evidence supports a hardware-deployable implementation.

jobs.latency_budget: offline / pre-run, bounded by product startup workflow
jobs.rationale: Target-independent preprocessing is best kept in software because it is file-oriented, transparent, and does not require deterministic hard real-time execution.
jobs.responsibility: Geometry ingestion and validation of DrivAerML STL input; normalize metadata and prepare reference geometry artifacts for downstream use.

jobs.rationale: Velocity selection, validation, and run setup are control-plane functions suited to firmware/host software and should remain transparent and referenceable.
jobs.responsibility: Operating-point management and envelope enforcement for stream velocity inputs across 20 to 55 m/s; prepare run configuration and maintain traceability.

jobs.latency_budget: application-defined; expected external-service latency with timeout supervision
jobs.rationale: The qualified model explicitly requires a remote GPU worker; there is no evidence that the surrogate is hardware-deployable, so it stays in GPU/CPU software.
jobs.responsibility: Execute the NVIDIA DoMINO Automotive Aero surrogate workflow for physics-based aerodynamic estimation and control-relevant response generation.

jobs.rationale: The reference path is explicitly for transparency and validation, not latency-critical actuation, so it belongs in software.
jobs.responsibility: Run the transparent reference path for calibration, comparison, and validation against surrogate outputs; preserve deterministic traceability to the reference workflow.

jobs.latency_budget: deterministic, one-cycle or registered synchronous behavior
jobs.rationale: These are the FPGA-appropriate hard real-time safety functions required by the contract and architecture; they are bounded, deterministic, and do not require surrogate compute in RTL.
jobs.responsibility: Hardware safety supervisor implementing stale-data rejection, timeout detection, command clamping, safe fallback selection, and bounded actuator output staging.

jobs.rationale: The selected FPGA prototype includes a soft CPU; firmware is the correct layer for orchestration, traceability, and interaction with the external model service.
jobs.responsibility: Soft-CPU supervision and product orchestration: issue requests, manage sequence numbers, monitor status, log faults, retry or degrade gracefully, and coordinate safe-state behavior.

jobs.rationale: Partitioning is implementation-agnostic and should optimize for the current FPGA prototype while preserving possible reuse; fpga_or_asic captures the reusable control-shell nature without claiming surrogate hardware deployment.
jobs.responsibility: System partitioning and integration of data handling, model transport, supervision, and command generation into a single product flow with clear software/hardware boundaries.

jobs.latency_budget: microseconds to low milliseconds, bounded by external service interaction
jobs.rationale: Transport integrity and framing are hardware-friendly but not the surrogate itself; this is exactly the kind of bounded logic suited to RTL.
jobs.responsibility: Model transport bridge on FPGA for compact request/response framing, sequence tagging, length checking, and handshake integrity with the external model service.

jobs.rationale: Optimization spans software, firmware, and RTL parameters and is best handled as a host-side compile/analysis loop rather than fixed hardware.
jobs.responsibility: Architecture optimization loop over latency, memory, and resource limits; tune firmware/hardware partitioning, control cadence, and transport parameters while preserving safety requirements.

jobs.rationale: Acceptance testing must observe the full system behavior, compare against reference outputs, and produce artifacts; software is the appropriate execution environment.
jobs.responsibility: Validation and acceptance testing across operating range, stale-command rejection, command bounding, timeout-to-safe fallback, and deterministic traceability.

firmware_gate.reason: Finalize CPU/host, bus, address map, interrupts, and register-map version before deployable firmware generation.

tradeoffs: Keeping the surrogate external preserves fidelity and transparency but adds service latency and dependency on GPU availability.
FPGA hardware safety supervision improves determinism and fault containment, but it does not reduce surrogate execution latency.
A soft-CPU + RTL safety shell is more portable and verifiable than a full hardware model implementation, at the cost of higher system integration complexity.
Software-based reference execution improves traceability and validation coverage, but it does not provide production-time actuation speed.
Future ASIC reuse could capture the bounded safety/control path, but the current evidence does not justify committing the surrogate to ASIC or FPGA compute.
Using compact metadata streams instead of full payload exposure simplifies RTL and I/O, but requires firmware/software to manage bulk data and model context off-chip.
